Organolead trihalide perovskite materials have been successfully used as light absorbers in efficient photovoltaic cells. Two different cell structures, based on mesoscopic metal oxides and planar heterojunctions have already demonstrated very impressive advances in performance. Here, we report a bilayer architecture comprising the key features of mesoscopic and planar structures obtained by a fully solution-based process. We used CH 3NH3 Pb(I 1 x Br x ) 3 ( x D 0.1-0.15) as the absorbing layer and poly(triarylamine) as a hole-transporting material.

Organolead trihalide perovskite materials have been successfully used as light absorbers in efficient photovoltaic cells. Two different cell structures, based on mesoscopic metal oxides and planar heterojunctions have already demonstrated very impressive advances in performance. Here, we report a bilayer architecture comprising the key features of mesoscopic and planar structures obtained by a fully solution-based process. We used CH 3NH3 Pb(I 1 x Br x ) 3 ( x D 0.1-0.15) as the absorbing layer and poly(triarylamine) as a hole-transporting material.
